gap: No result ChatGPT got states the five-year cost of the box plus electricity, worked out from today's prices on the makers' own stores and the EIA's August 2026 US home electricity rate. The figures are UGREEN DH2300 about $349, TerraMaster F2-425 about $445 and UGREEN DXP2800 about $520. The F2-425 is $120 cheaper to buy than the DXP2800 but only about $75 cheaper over five years, because it is rated at 22 W against 16.38 W.
standout_why: ComputingForGeeks (2026-10-24), which ChatGPT cited in two chats, already gives each model's yearly running cost. It uses the makers' access ratings and an assumed $0.20/kWh: DH2300 $24.04, DS223j $28.58, DXP2800 $28.70, F2-425 $38.54. It also gives a five-year power gap for the DXP2800 GT against the DXP2800. It does not add the yearly cost to today's purchase prices for the models under $300, and its prices are from Amazon on Oct 24. Starry Hope gives only a general rule (10 W ≈ 88 kWh ≈ $16 a year) and no figure for any model. nas.kuibu.net gives no wattage or running cost. So rivals already have the yearly power cost. What is new is the five-year total at today's prices and the EIA rate, and that is a modest addition.
decides: The finding makes the F2-425 look like less of a bargain than ChatGPT suggests, but it does not change the order at maker-store prices. DH2300 ($349) < F2-425 ($445) < DXP2800 ($520). If the $296.99 Walmart DXP2800 listing that ChatGPT showed is real (not checked here), the DXP2800's five-year total would be $296.99 + $130.29 = $427.28. That would beat the F2-425 at $269.99 ($444.98), which flips ChatGPT's main 'TerraMaster F2-425 for value' pick. These figures assume the maker's access-power rating for all 8,760 hours of the year, which is the worst case. Ocinside measured the DXP2800 at about 7 W idle, less than half its rated 16.38 W.
